service_procedures.safety_warning: A new item with unconnected sense leads will report those inputs as out of range if commissioning is asserted incorrectly. Do not attempt to command the contactors closed at any point in this procedure. If the item does not behave as described, stop and escalate rather than continuing.
steps: Confirm the item is not fitted in a pack or is fitted with all cables disconnected
Connect the service supply and confirm the supply indication
Connect the sense leads one module at a time, confirming the cell count after each
Assert commissioning and confirm that contactor actuation is inhibited
Read the configuration identification and confirm it resolves to the configuration this item should carry
Release commissioning, remove the service tool and confirm the item is inert
service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A commissioning technician trained on this procedure. In this corpus that role is fictional and no training exists.

service_procedures.safety_warning: A replaced slave runs on the previous slave's calibration table until it is recalibrated. Do not return the vehicle to service between replacement and recalibration: in that interval the item reports cell values it has not measured.
steps: Capture the event log before disconnecting anything
Isolate the high-voltage system by the vehicle's own means and confirm it
Disconnect the slave and replace it
Recalibrate the affected sensor tables against a reference measurement
Verify the cell count and the values against the pack's build record
Perform the post-service check
service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A service technician trained on this procedure

service_procedures.procedure_name: Read and clear a latched fault
service_procedures.safety_warning: Clearing a latched fault without removing its cause returns the vehicle to service with the condition intact. The item will latch again, but the vehicle may have been driven in between.
steps: Capture the event log
Record every active diagnosis entry and its severity before clearing any
Determine whether the condition that raised the entry is still present
Clear the entry only if the condition is absent
Perform the post-service check
service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A service technician trained on this procedure

service_procedures.safety_warning: Reprogramming without restoring the parameter values leaves the item on whatever values were previously in memory, which may belong to a different pack. Read the parameter values back and compare them against the specification before returning to service.
steps: Capture the event log and record the current configuration identification
Confirm the replacement image is the released build and not a development image
Reprogram and verify by readback
Restore every parameter value from the calibration specification
Perform the post-service check and confirm the configuration identification still resolves
tools_required: Commissioning tool with the released identity
service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A service technician trained on this procedure and authorised for reprogramming

service_procedures.post_service_check: None; this procedure is the post-service check
service_procedures.safety_warning: The fault injection is performed through the service interface and the vehicle must be stationary with the high-voltage system isolated. Do not perform this check with the vehicle in motion or with the pack energised.
steps: Confirm the item's state and that no safety-severity entry is active other than the one being worked
Inject a fault through the service interface and confirm the item reaches and confirms the safe state within the fault-tolerant time interval
Confirm the configuration identification resolves to exactly one released configuration
Record the result
service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: Any technician who has completed one of SVC-01 to SVC-04

required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
